original_question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with biliary atresia in Egyptian infants located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with biliary atresia in Egyptian infants located?
final_qi.long_answer: Studies in Egyptian infants with biliary atresia have shown a significant association with promoter polymorphisms of the interleukin-18 (IL18) gene. IL18 is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 11 (11q22-q23); hence the gene implicated in the Egyptian cohort resides on chromosome 11.

final_answer.long_answer: Genetic studies in Egyptian infants with biliary atresia identified risk variants in the ADD3 (adducin-3) gene. ADD3 maps to cytogenetic band 10q24.2 on chromosome 10, making chromosome 10 the locus associated with the disease in this population.
